messages:
sam: heads-up — we're seeing a jump in preemptible evictions in europe-west3 for the spot pool. eviction rate +15% over the last 10m, p99 latency for gen routes ~3x. backlog on async queue mounting.

alice: copying. do we have a cause? noisy auction or provider-level maintenance?

raj: looks like auction noise. cloud metrics show simultaneous price spikes in eu-west3-b/c. I can confirm the eviction events show the usual 'preemptible' tag.

kevin: any customers impacted? are hosted API calls failing or just slower?

sam: majority are increased tail latency; some short 503s for requests that hit a shard that lost GPUs mid-request. So client retries mitigated most failures but you can see increased cost from retries.

sre-oncall: infra-bot alerted at 1799989600. infra-bot: "spot-eviction-detector: rule europe-west3 evictions > 10% triggered".

infra-bot: "autoscaler: currently 80% of pool is spot, on-demand capacity 20%. fallback-policy: mix-pool-fallback (preempted -> attempt on-demand up to 30% of baseline)."

alice: propose immediate temporary policy change: raise on-demand fallback cap to 40% for eu-west3 to reduce tail latency. keep spot mix for cost but reduce risk.

raj: +1. also reduce batch size for gen endpoints to lower p99 when instances switch. suggest: set batch_size_max to 12 -> 6 for eu-west3.

kevin: can we do a targeted rollout for only high-latency routes (api/llm/generate) instead of all routes? want to avoid raising cost for embedding-heavy customers.

sam: yes — route-level policy exists. plan: 1) bump fallback cap to 40% for eu-west3 2) set reduced batching for /v1/generate routes in that region 3) watch for evictions to drop below 5% before rolling down.

alice: I can push the routing change. patch:```yaml
region: europe-west3
fallback: on_demand
fallback_cap_percent: 40
targets:
  - route: /v1/generate
    batch_size_max: 6
```

raj: rolling that now via safe-rollout 2 -> 10 -> 50 nodes. keeping canary on a small subset first. command: `infractl rollout apply europe-west3 -f patch.yaml --canary=2`

infra-bot: "rollout started: canary 2 nodes (eu-west3). monitoring eviction_rate, p99_latency, on_demand_util."

kevin: suggest also enabling short-term retry budget of +1 for clients to reduce immediate 503 surface area. adjust gateway retry to 2 -> 3 for 30s window.

sre-oncall: done. gateway retries increased for eu-west3. watching for client-side amplification.

sam: quick note on cost: expect on-demand usage to rise ~30-40% of baseline while this is on. I'll estimate delta in cost channel once we stabilize.

alice: can someone run `kubectl get pods -l pool=spot-eu -o jsonpath='{.items[*].metadata.annotations.eviction_ts}'` and paste if there's a correlated timestamp cluster?

raj: pasted snippet from control plane logs: "eviction_ts: [1799989005,1799989010,1799989018,1799989050]" — clustered within 60s for several AZs.

kevin: that cluster suggests auction-wave. we should add a tie-breaker policy to prefer routing live requests to on-demand when a pool reports >=10 evictions in 1m. avoids serving to a pool that's mid-wave.

sam: good idea. add rule: `if evictions_1m >= 10 -> mark pool degraded for 90s and prefer on-demand` — low-risk and reversible.

alice: I'll add that rule to the decision engine and include a metric alert for 'pool_degraded_by_eviction' so we can track reoccurrence.

infra-bot: "decision-engine: rule applied (eviction-wave-tiebreaker). pools will be deprioritized for 90s when triggered."

raj: monitoring shows p99 dropping already in the canary group. evictions still spiking in certain AZs but routing change looks to have reduced client-visible latency.

kevin: great. can we set an automated rollback window of 30m if cost delta > +20% vs baseline? want cost guardrails.

sam: yes — adding an automation: rollback-if-cost-increase >20% in 30m. will need a manual override for enterprise incidents.

alice: pushed automation and alert. documentation note: will add postmortem template entry: cause=auction-wave, mitigations=on_demand_fallback+batch_reduce+tiebreaker, cost_impact_estimate.

raj: action items: (1) monitor for 60m, (2) collect 1h cost delta, (3) start postmortem if evictions persist after 2h.

kevin: thumbs-up. thanks team. I'll notify CS for any customers who saw higher latencies.

sre-oncall: leaving a note in incidents channel and pinning the rollout links.

sam: closing the loop — we'll keep the temporary changes until the eviction rate normalizes and then slowly ramp back to baseline spot mix. thanks everyone :thumbsup:"
